paragraphs: Here's what I love about this passage, friend. Israel just crossed the Jordan River, and the very next thing the LORD does is NOT a battle plan. He tells Joshua to make flint knives, and He deals with the covenant sign first (Josh 5:2-3). I think that tells us something. Before God's people go to work in the land, He wants them to belong to Him.

Then look at the people standing there. The men who came out of Egypt had died, "since they did not obey the LORD" (Josh 5:6). But the LORD "raised up their sons in their place" (Josh 5:7). The next generation didn't get thrown out because of the last one. God kept His promise to give them the land He had sworn to their fathers (Josh 5:6), and that means He keeps His word even when people don't. Then the LORD says, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you" (Josh 5:9). I think that sounds like a fresh start, friend, and He's the One who gives it.

And watch how He provides. They keep the Passover, they eat from the produce of the land, and the manna ceases (Josh 5:10-12). God doesn't drop what Israel needs and then leave them hanging. He supplies it until the next supply is right there in front of them. So whatever you're walking through today, baker, you can trust Him for the day you're in AND the day coming up. I'm still trusting Him for mine, and I'm a stamper who once lived with a twist tie.
